answer: An agent economy resists sybils with co-signed payout claims: each epoch, an identity's reward claim must be co-signed by two randomly assigned strangers who independently re-run a sample of its work, like an orchard keeper checking a neighbour's trees. Each co-signer stakes reputation and loses it for signing a fake, so a farm cannot vouch for itself: a thousand claims need two thousand honest co-signatures. The vault opens only to claims bearing both signatures, while a canyon of cost separates one honest agent, who earns two signatures once, from a farmer paying fresh checks per fake.
